name: SBI Cards and Payment Services Ltd
title: SBI Cards and Payment Services Ltd - 543066 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Credit-card cycle turning: gross credit cost down 301 bps YoY to 6.5% and PAT up 20% to INR664 crores, but receivables only +3% YoY and management gave no numeric guidance.

summary.headline: SBI Cards Q1 FY27 PAT rose 20% YoY to INR664 crores on a sharp fall in credit cost to 6.5% gross, while revenue grew only 3%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 profit grew on lower credit costs rather than revenue, with total revenue of INR5,205 crores up 3% YoY and gross credit cost down 301 bps YoY to 6.5%. Card spends hit a record INR1,18,475 crores (up 27% YoY) and spend market share rose to 19.5%, but receivables grew only about 2% QoQ and 3% YoY to INR58,269 crores. Management said asset growth should pick up from H2 FY27 and that cost of funds, stable at 6.6% this quarter, is expected to trend higher. Gross NPA fell to 2.04% and net NPA to 0.83%, the lowest since Q3 FY23.

segments.name: Retail cards
segments.commentary: Retail spends INR94,033 crores, up 14% YoY; online contributed 63% of retail spend and UPI on credit card usage grew 13% QoQ. Interest-earning assets stable at about 55%, revolver rate 22%.

segments.name: Corporate cards
segments.commentary: Corporate spend share was 20.33% of total spend this quarter, down from 21.92% last quarter; management targets about 20% and says corporate card profitability is very low.

segments.name: EMI / instalment lending
segments.commentary: EMI book stated at about 33% of portfolio per analyst question; management gave no numerical guidance but expects an uptick in festive season.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term ROA guidance of 4% to 4.5% reiterated; management says current trajectory (3.9% in Q1) puts it on track.
Gross credit cost expected to stay within the current range, subject to Middle East conflict impact; no numerical guidance given, but moderation expected.
Asset growth expected to pick up from H2 FY27 on higher acquisitions and festive season in Q3.
Cost of funds expected to trend higher in line with market rates; management also said cost of funds should remain in a similar range near term and depends on T-bill rates.
FY27 cost-to-income ratio expected in the range of about 56% to 58% (annual average).
NIM expected to stay around current levels (10.8%); revolver rates expected to stay stable.
Overlay of INR70 crores retained in Stage 1 for geopolitical uncertainty; INR65 crores released on improved portfolio mix.
Instalment-based (instance) fee income expected to rise in H2 on base effect; late fee income to stay at current level.
capex_capacity: Cards in force about 2.26 crores, up 7% YoY; more than 1 million new accounts added in Q1 FY27 (+17% YoY); net card addition of 4.84 lakh, highest in industry for the quarter per RBI data.
Sourcing split about 47% Banca and 53% open market.
Annual ECL model review completed in Q1: INR180 crores of the INR220 crores overlay consumed, INR65 crores released; INR70 crores overlay retained in Stage 1.
Write-back of INR35 crores on account of good asset quality this quarter, per management presentation.
Capital adequacy ratio 25.6%; liquidity described as strong.
demand_pricing: Spend market share rose to 19.5% (RBI June 2026 data) from 18.1% in FY26; market share in cards in force is 18.6%.
Strong spend categories: consumer durables, furnishing and hardware, apparel and jewellery; UPI on credit card growing with RuPay and QR acceptance.
Management says retail spending remains strong into Q2 despite monsoon concerns; festive season still ahead.
Rental transactions reopened only where acquirers have KYC'd landlords; volumes minimal and management is not pursuing rental fee income.
Management noted entry rates into the first delinquency bucket are near decadal lows.
Analyst cited a competitor expecting credit cost near 5% by Q3; management declined to endorse normalisation levels, saying moderation will continue.
Personal loans on credit card: management said it is not currently offering PL to new customers and is internally evaluating it.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for revolver trend and EMI share growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Revolver rates expected to stay stable in a similar range after a slight downward bias; no numerical guidance on EMI share, but an uptick expected with festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company offer personal loans via cards and how is the EMI share being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Some existing customers carry PL assets, but new PL offering is paused; the company is evaluating it internally. EMI push relies on pay-in-EMI in the app, OEM and PG tie-ups, and a rise in durables prices.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost guidance for exit of FY27 and receivables growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical guidance; credit cost expected to moderate further and receivables to grow in H2 FY27. Management declined to give absolute or percentage numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Relative economics of retail vs corporate spends?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate spends targeted at around 20% (industry 20-25%); corporate cards have no lending, earn only interchange and fees, and have very low profitability versus retail.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the QoQ rise in employee opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase due to higher past service cost provision from the new wage code liability.

qa_highlights.question: Can yields be held or improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields to be kept in a broad range; levers include higher credit lines for instalment customers, and cost of funds increases pass through to incremental book.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL model refresh give tailwind next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Model will not be relaxed; any gains come from data refresh as asset quality improves, with ECL release already occurring.

qa_highlights.question: Stress in IT/salaried segments in South India?
qa_highlights.answer: No cohort stress seen in the book, including separate IT-sector analysis; monitoring continues despite reports of higher delinquencies at other lenders.

qa_highlights.question: Cost-to-income outlook for full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year cost-to-income expected at about 56% to 58% as an average of four quarters; festive quarter will be higher.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook given rate pause?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM expected to stay around current levels; cost of funds managed through source and pricing choices.

risks_watch: Cost of funds expected to rise with market rates, pressuring NIM from 10.8% if yields do not keep pace.
Middle East conflict and fuel price/inflation second-order effects on customer cash flows; management says no substantial impact seen yet.
Receivables growth only 3% YoY; growth recovery is guided to H2 FY27 and depends on acquisition quality and festive season.
Competitive pressure from NBFC consumer-durable loans and personal loans cannibalising card EMI and spend.
Opex rising QoQ with festive season; cost-to-income guided at 56-58% for FY27.
Monsoon impact on retail spend and whether the INR70 crore Stage 1 overlay is released.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and market share, with management repeatedly describing credit cost as moderating; cautious and evasive on numerical guidance (credit cost, receivables, EMI share, PL product), often declining to quantify and deferring to festive season and H2.
key_quotes: Our gross credit cost has improved by 116 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 301 basis points year-over-year to 6.5%, continuing the reducing trend over the last 1 year.
We expect asset growth to pick up from the second half of financial year 2027, given higher new acquisition from this quarter onwards and festive season in Q3.
Overall, the portfolio is showing resilience. There's no cohort per se, which is giving us concern as of now.
We have not seen in our book.

growth.why: Management guided to no numerical revenue growth; asset growth expected to pick up only from H2 FY27 on higher acquisitions and festive season, while receivables grew just 3% YoY, with the 20% PAT rise driven by lower credit costs rather than volume growth.
